title: The Hard Thing About Hard Things
author: Ben Horowitz

lessons.title: There Is No Recipe for Hard Things
lessons.key_idea: Horowitz's near-collapse at Loudcloud shows that the hardest leadership problems have no formula, so you must learn to act without one.

lessons.title: Tell Your Team the Bad News
lessons.key_idea: Leaders who share bad news openly build the trust and shared problem-solving a company needs to survive a crisis.
issues: scene 2: The speech-bubble tail starts at the leader's shoulder and crosses his raised arm, so the arm and tail merge into one tangled line. The 'HOPE IT TURNS AROUND QUIETLY' label sits almost against the bottom edge of the bubble. (fix: Start the bubble tail at the head/mouth area, clear of the arm lines, or move the bubble up and right so the tail does not cross the arm. Move the label at least 24px below the bubble.)

scene 1: The two connector lines from the Loudcloud cloud run down through the customer crowd and pass over the people icons. The crowd figures also overlap each other, which makes that cluster hard to read. (fix: End the connector lines at the top of the crowd, or at the ground line beside it. Space the customer figures so their heads and bodies do not overlap.)

lessons.title: Lead Bullets, Not Silver Bullets
lessons.key_idea: When you are losing, there is no clever shortcut, so you must do the hard, unglamorous work of making your product better.
issues: scene 1: In 'THE LEGEND' card the monster face sits off-centre to the right, and the left half of the card is empty. No silver bullet is visible, so the card does not show 'a single silver bullet could stop a monster'. The bullet looks missing, or it animated out before the final frame. (fix: Keep a silver (indigo) bullet visible in the final frame on the left of the card, aimed at the monster, possibly with a short motion trail. Alternatively, centre the monster and place the bullet beside it so the composition is balanced and the legend is readable.)

lessons.title: Lay People Off the Right Way
lessons.key_idea: If you must cut jobs, move fast, own the decision yourself, and treat every departing person with respect, because everyone who stays is watching.
issues: scene 5: The speech bubble above the two figures in the 'YOUR MANAGER' panel is empty. It looks like missing text or a broken element. (fix: Put short text in the bubble (e.g. 'I'M SORRY' or 'LET'S TALK'), sized at least 18px and in amber to match the outline. If you don't want text, replace it with three dots.)

lessons.title: People, Products, Profits, in That Order
lessons.key_idea: Making your company a good place to work, including real training for employees, is what makes great products and profits possible.

lessons.title: Peacetime CEO Versus Wartime CEO
lessons.key_idea: Calm times call for a broad, consensus-building leader, while existential threats call for a focused, decisive one, and great leaders know which moment they are in.

lessons.title: Mastering the Struggle Within
lessons.key_idea: The leader's hardest battle is psychological, and surviving it means keeping your eyes on the path forward rather than on the wall you fear hitting.

plan.title: The Hard Thing About Hard Things
plan.author: Ben Horowitz
plan.confidence_note: I know this book's main arguments, its Loudcloud and Opsware story, and its signature frameworks in solid detail, though not every anecdote word for word.
plan.one_liner: No management book can save you when everything breaks. Here is how leaders survive anyway.
plan.summary: Ben Horowitz co-founded Loudcloud, a cloud services company that nearly died when the dot-com bubble burst. He led it through layoffs, a tough public offering, and a dramatic reinvention as the software company Opsware, which was later sold to Hewlett-Packard. This book is his honest account of that ride and the lessons it taught him. Horowitz argues that most business advice covers the easy problems, while the hard ones have no formula. Examples include firing a friend, laying off staff, or keeping going when the company might fail. He shares practical guidance on telling the truth to your team, fixing problems the slow way, letting people go with dignity, and putting people first. He also explains how to switch between calm and crisis leadership. Above all, he describes the inner struggle every leader faces, and how to keep going through it.
